content: 1. Norgestimate and Norgestrel: Cobicistat and atazanavir can increase the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme, which affects hepatic and intestinal metabolism. This may increase the risk of adverse effects. Alternatives should be considered if available, and close monitoring is recommended. 2. Nortriptyline: Atazanavir and cobicistat can elevate nortriptyline levels through unspecified mechanisms. Careful dose titration of the antidepressant is advised, starting with the lowest feasible dose and monitoring for therapeutic response during coadministration. 3. Olaparib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase olaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily with moderate inhibitors, and to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily with strong inhibitors. Do not substitute tablets for capsules. 4. Oliceridine: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification may be required, including less frequent dosing. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dose to achieve stable effects. 5. Omaveloxolone: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day if unavoidable. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects occur. 6. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Cobicistat increases the levels of this combination by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and coadministration is contraindicated. Atazanavir also increases levels, requiring therapy modification. Administer atazanavir 300 mg (without ritonavir) in the morning when coadministered with Viekira Pak. 7. Omeprazole: Omeprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Avoid coadministration or limit the proton pump inhibitor (PPI) dose to omeprazole 20 mg, taken 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive patients. PPIs are not recommended for treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 8. Ondansetron: Atazanavir and cobicistat increase ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as CYP450 inhibitors may reduce ondansetron clearance. 9. Orlistat: Orlistat decreases atazanavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 10. Osilodrostat: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase osilodrostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Osimertinib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase osimertinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternatives exist, monitor closely for adverse effects. 12. Ospemifene: Atazanavir and cobicistat increase ospemifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative anticonvulsants or antiretroviral therapies. Monitor for loss of virologic response if coadministration is necessary. 14. Oxybutynin: Atazanavir increases oxybutynin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 15. Oxycodone: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase oxycodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the oxycodone dose if necessary. Monitor closely for toxicity. 16. Ozanimod: Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 17. Paclitaxel: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 18. Pacritinib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase pacritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Palbociclib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day if unavoidable. 20. Palovarotene: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase palovarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 21. Panobinostat: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Pantoprazole: Pantoprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Avoid coadministration or limit PPI doses to omeprazole-equivalent levels in treatment-naive patients. PPIs are not recommended for treatment-experienced patients. 23. Paricalcitol: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase paricalcitol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for toxicity. 24. Paroxetine: Cobicistat increases paroxetine levels through unspecified mechanisms. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor closely during coadministration. 25. Pazopanib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase pazopanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day if unavoidable. 26. Pexidartinib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase pexidartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the pexidartinib dose if unavoidable. 27. Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases atazanavir and cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases atazanavir and cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Pimavanserin: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase pimavanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if unavoidable. 30. Pimozide: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to a risk of QT prolongation. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Pindolol: Atazanavir increases pindolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 32. Pioglitazone: Atazanavir increases pioglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 33. Pirtobrutinib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg if unavoidable. 34. Pitavastatin: Atazanavir increases pitavastatin levels through an unknown mechanism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Polatuzumab Vedotin: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for toxicity. 36. Pomalidomide: Atazanavir increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 37. Ponatinib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 38. Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases atazanavir and cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 39. Pralsetinib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 40. Pramlintide: Atazanavir may reduce pramlintide effects due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 41. Pravastatin: Cobicistat increases pravastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Start with the lowest recommended dose and monitor for safety. 42. Praziquantel: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Prednisolone and Prednisone: Atazanavir increases prednisolone and prednisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Primidone: Primidone decreases atazanavir and cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 45. Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, Natural): Cobicistat and atazanavir increase progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 46. Propafenone: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase propafenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Protriptyline: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase protriptyline levels through unspecified mechanisms. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose and monitor closely. 48. Quazepam: Cobicistat increases quazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Quetiapine: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose if unavoidable. 50. Quinidine: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
